entry_points.text: The collection is parameterized input to an external driver that selects encoding by mode, builds directly or via per-vector callbacks, supplies linear and fragment bytes, executes classic or internal semantics and compares observed length and value pairs.

Generator callbacks are deferred entries synthesizing register, shift distance, magnitude, atomic and branch combinations at run time, including repeated updates and maximal constructions, so the table stores only a builder reference.

exports.text: This slice contributes self checking entries to a shared filter machine table over arithmetic, logic, shifts, branches, memory, atomics and packet loads in classic and internal encodings, each joining a label with an inline sequence or generator reference plus attributes and expected outcomes runnable without further context.

hazards.text: Interpreter and compiled behavior must agree on pinned gates, finals and sign extension of large immediates and masks; any just in time divergence fails, with verifier zero extension preserved.
A load just below ancillary base passes checking yet yields zero at runtime, so validation success does not imply runtime success and callers must tolerate post acceptance failure.
All-ones must stay unsigned where it also reads as -1, so unsigned self division yields 1 and narrow ops discard high bits first; signed handling, traps or missing truncation give wrong results.

Boundary shifts at 0, near, exactly and beyond word size plus sign-set and host order edges need halves assertions and conditional offsets, not host shift behavior. Unaligned and large accesses are valid with neighbors preserved; out of bounds reads take zero path without outside access; zero divisors terminate with zero.
Stack depth must cover accessed slots such as 40 below frame or 8 bytes for atomics and be enforced before execution; large regions need large memory marking.

Oversized and special spanning programs are expected invalid argument failures, while tail packet edges strictly accept the final octet and reject wider overruns and link layer pairs split in-bounds acceptance from out-of-bounds zero.

invariants.text: Positive internal vectors use internal mode with empty input and one expectation on channel zero. They seed general registers, apply arithmetic, logical, shift or move operations in immediate and register forms, then use equality branches that fall through on success and exit early on mismatch with distinct success versus mismatch codes.

Staged gates pin exact totals: addition requires 4063, 12177, 36518, 109540, 328605, 985799 for final 2957380; subtraction seeds 0-9, gates -55, chains subtract 10 then negates for 11; multiplication seeds 11 then 1-9, gates 439084800 with halves checked; repeated self subtract and self exclusive-or must yield zero for final 1.

Move and long immediate vectors propagate all-ones 64-bit down the chain, clear with width specific zeros, accumulate plus a constant for shared 0xfefe. Mixed divide and modulo gate before -1. Register counted logical and arithmetic shifts use mid gates before -1. On 32-bit only, zero context stays zero and nonzero shows zero upper for final 1.

Classic scratch has sixteen word cells 0-15 writable from index and readable into arithmetic. Vectors fill all cells then sum, or walk slots storing index, reloading, converting accumulator to index, incrementing onward. One long halfword absolute load vector over Ethernet plus IP plus UDP shape expects length 88 and value 0x001b.

Classic execution uses accumulator plus index with load, store, exchange, arithmetic and return; internal uses general registers with R0 as result and explicit exit. 32-bit results keep low half and clear upper; 64-bit immediate moves sign extend negatives. Sign moves propagate 8, 16, 32-bit signs, with 32-bit form zero padding upper and 64-bit form extending fully.

Add, subtract and multiply wrap modulo width: 32-bit discards carry while 64-bit retains wide results including multiply halves. Full width constants materialize in one step with halves verified via shifts, including values beyond 32 bits. 64-bit immediates cover checker output, positive with zero, negative with zero, and positive with negative mixes.

Unsigned divide and remainder cover narrow and wide widths with register and immediate divisors, including small quotients, near-maximum dividends with residues 0, 1, 2, and all-ones divided by itself yielding 1. Signed forms reuse unsigned operations with offset selector 1, e.g. -6 divided by 2 is -3 and -7 remainder 2 is -1.

Bitwise and, or and exclusive-or cover narrow and wide widths with register and immediate operands. Narrow forms clear destination upper half; wide immediate forms sign extend the operand before combining, verified by low word plus full width register comparisons.

32-bit logical shifts cover zero identity, single bit, near width and hex patterns with zero fill truncated to 32 bits. 64-bit shifts are checked via halves across 0, below 32, exactly 32 and above 32 including counts 0,1,12,31,32,36. Arithmetic right shift replicates sign across the same edges; negation exchanges 3 and -3 in both widths.

Endian conversion spans 16, 32, 64-bit widths with big and little endian sources over complementary 64-bit patterns, checking 64-bit directly and after 32-bit downshift and 32-bit combined with shifted copy for clear upper. Byte swap mirrors coverage by reversing low 16, 32, 64 bits with halves exposed and clear upper checks.

Loads cover byte, halfword, word and doubleword from frame and data bases. Narrow loads zero extend while sign extending loads propagate source high bit. Frame uses negative offsets differing by host order plus negative, small and large positive and unaligned displacements with large memory marking. Same register may serve as destination and base with small reservation.

Partial narrow stores change only addressed bytes, confirmed by full cell readback with clear and set high bits. Immediate and register stores across all widths round trip through matching loads at deep frame displacement, including all low bits set and only high bit clear boundaries.

Atomics span word and doubleword across plain, fetch augmented, exchange and compare exchange with add, and, or, exclusive-or, symmetric per width with register pairing and magnitude pattern runs without packet data. Memory holds combined result, fetch returns prior value, non-fetch leaves update operand observable, wide halves folded into outcome.

Compare exchange compares R0 against a frame slot; on equality the source is stored, prior memory stays in R0 in both outcomes, mismatch leaves memory unchanged, repeat observes updated memory and source is preserved. Coverage uses per width success return, success store, failed return, failed store and source preservation vectors; xor-fetch and exchange use four vectors per width with frame pointer unchanged.

Preservation requires 32-bit arithmetic and word atomics to keep source upper halves, checked with wide patterns reduced so disturbance yields nonzero, and 32-bit branches in all conditions and operand forms to leave full width operands untouched. Families preload ten distinct seeds, operate on R8 or R9, then require all seeds intact before success, so helpers stay transparent.

Branches validate equality, inequality, bit presence and unsigned plus signed ordering in 32 and 64-bit immediate and register forms, unsigned near top of range versus signed negatives, strict versus non-strict, not-taken before taken so errors clear the result. Coverage sweeps magnitudes with pattern runs plus static all-clear, all-set, extreme and self compare fixed outcomes and sign extension agreement checks.

Wide immediates occupy two slots and displacements account for skipping one or two wides, landing on exit or selecting low-bit variants. Short forward jumps check offsets 0-4 from cleared result for cleared outcome. Long conditionals separate runtime taken, runtime not taken, always and never taken. Shifts iterate all distances with aliasing; magnitudes iterate all classes with repeats.

Absolute loads read 1, 2 or 4 octets in network order with unaligned support; indirect adds index to displacement before the same checked read. In-bounds returns via accumulator; overruns take zero path with reduced length. Tail defines per width edge with final octet accepted and wider overruns rejected, plus default index, linear plus fragment mix, repeated index reuse and link layer shift.

Multiply shift load keeps low nibble of the octet, scales by four into index and leaves accumulator unchanged; out of range and raw negative yield zero while link layer matches direct scaled nibble. Accumulator and index start zero, so add and subtract preserve or negate, multiply yields zero, cleared divide yields zero and equality on cleared registers takes the branch.

Outcomes pair a selector with numeric return for direct checks and boolean pass markers. Preservation expects zero difference and functional expects success; constant decision and long jump cases vary the second value among 0, 1, 2 for never taken, taken or fall through.

state_machines.text: Validation rejects missing return, immediate divide by zero, socket disallowed ops, scratch spills, index only returns, raw negative displacements, ancillary base plus maximum loads, oversized programs and special spanning jumps with invalid argument and no execution, while maximal gap, long, edge, context, call and literal heavy programs succeed.

Internal flow is initialize, compute, compare, exit: seed including wide loads, run the operation, branch to success versus failure return and terminate. Exit ignores trailing ops, unconditional jumps skip to success, forward skips and backward loops appear, and chained signed walks require every decision correct.

Classic flow is preset, fetch, return: optionally preset index, fetch 1, 2 or 4 bytes absolute or indexed from linear or fragment data, then return accumulator. Zero index divisor halts with zero; out of range fetches take the zero path.

structs.text: Each entry joins a label with classic or internal inline code or a generator reference, mode plus no-data, expected-fail, fragment and large memory modifiers, sparse packet octet map, ordered length and value pairs, and optional fragment bytes, error code, stack reservation and repeat counts, with internal marker and empty slots.

R0 carries result and exit with low 32 bits compared on channel zero; R1 carries counts or bases; R2 and R3 carry expectations; R1-R4 provide setup; R10 is frame base for negative offsets with equality skipping two ops. Widths cover byte, halfword, word, doubleword and 16, 32, 64-bit conversion with depths such as 8 and 40 and offsets such as 0, 8, 256, 512, 4096.

Categories distinguish classic versus internal execution, byte, halfword and word fetch widths, absolute versus indirect addressing, return sources, general registers, absent data, expected failure and fragmented input, plus atomic fetch versus non-fetch with endian dependent narrow displacements. Invalid argument is the rejection code for bad displacements and ancillary base plus maximum.
